frames.narration: Node 1 has learned something: node 9 has failed. Nobody else knows yet. There is no central server to tell the others.
Round 1: node 1 picks two random peers (the fanout is 2) and tells them.
Round 2: nodes 1, 2 and 3 each pick random peers. Now node 2 tells node 4, and node 3 tells node 5. Three nodes became five informed.
The number of informed nodes roughly doubles each round, so a cluster of 1,000 nodes learns within about 10 rounds. Some messages go to nodes that already know, which is wasted but harmless.
If a message is lost, nothing special is needed. The node simply hears it from someone else a round or two later. That redundancy is what makes gossip robust.

states.n5: message lost, hears it next round

frames.narration: Every node did the same small amount of work per round, no node was a bottleneck, and no node was essential. The price is that for a few rounds, different nodes hold different views.
